newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa retreats from highs after bear raid.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa retreats from highs after bear raid.

text.p: London cocoa's attempt to break free from a rigid downtrend channel failed on Friday when a bear raid hammered prices from their highs, traders said.

Benchmark March cocoa had surged to 934 stg a tonne, surfacing above the trendline that has kept the market's borders well defined in the past month. Morning gains stemmed from follow-through buying and short covering.

But New York's weak performance quickly reversed the pattern, bringing in trade profit taking and price fixing from Ivorian shippers, pushing the March contract to a low of 916 stg. March finished the day at 925 stg a tonne, up three.
"London suffered a bear raid. But it closed quite strong so probably there is more buying to be done," said one trader.
Bear players were targeting a close around this week's low of 910 stg.
Other contracts closed narrowly mixed with December down two at 887 stg and May up two at 943. Volume on the Exchange reached 4,370 lots.

Traders dismissed Ghana's purchases which totalled 20,052 tonnes in the third week of the 1996/97 season ending October 31. The cumulative so far is 75,192 compared with 87,520 by the end of the fourth week ending November 2 in the previous season.
"We are keeping an eye on the figure. But it never does anything," said one trader.

News from Ghana also included a manifesto by the leading opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP) saying it will privatise cocoa exports and increase farmgate prices if it wins next month's presidential and general elections.
But political analysts are placing their bets on President Jerry Rawlings to win the elections.
Technical resistance is pegged at 930 basis March, but more seriously at 942-945. Support is at 910. --Clelia Oziel, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8072
